- **Pay:** A14 USD 37144–55134 annual, effective 2025-09-01

## EMST role: Field resource technician (state variant, entry level; P1)

*Match:* `skos:closeMatch`, confidence 0.55, unreviewed agent draft (`emst-x5-tx:R02-field-resource-technician/state:2688`). *Authority position (editorial):* resource-manager.

**Competency targets at this level (editorial draft target levels, agent-drafted)**

- Sample and assess vegetation using standardized field protocols — entry L1
- Detect and record wildlife by direct observation, sign and standardized surveys — entry L1
- Measure water quality and survey aquatic communities in the field — entry L1
- Identify organisms from field characters, specimens, images and recordings — entry L1
- Record field observations with protocol fidelity and data integrity — entry L1
- Manage field sample custody and field quality control — entry L1
- Navigate and travel safely in remote terrain with and without digital aids — entry L1
- Manage risk in uncontrolled field environments — entry L1
- Ground-truth remote-sensed, modelled and AI-generated outputs in the field — entry L1
- Describe, test and sample soils in the field — entry L1
- Provide first aid and emergency medical care in remote field settings — entry L1
- Collect trace-level and genetic environmental samples without contamination — entry L1
- Apply field biosecurity and decontamination protocols — entry L1
- Operate small boats and work safely on water in aquatic, coastal and marine field settings — entry L1
- Deploy, maintain and verify field sensor networks — entry L1
- Drive and operate field vehicles safely on unpaved roads and off road — entry L1
- Apply safety practices and stop-work authority across field, facility and incident settings — entry L1
- Interpret and question environmental data products in everyday work — entry L1
- Use AI tools responsibly in everyday environmental work — entry L1
- Validate AI-generated work products before professional use — entry L1
- Record provenance and AI involvement in work products — entry L1

**Main tasks at this level (agent draft, in record order)**

*% time: set by the supervisor; EMST supplies none before job analysis.*

*Critical and needed-at-entry tasks: Assessment pending (job analysis).*

- Establish vegetation monitoring plots to protocol and record species composition, cover and density within the program's measurement-quality objectives
- Identify plants on sample plots to the protocol's required taxonomic level, collecting labelled vouchers for any plant not identified with certainty
- Conduct point-count, transect or call-playback wildlife surveys to protocol, recording detections, distance bands and survey conditions
- Identify wildlife sign such as tracks, scat, nests and feeding remains to species or group, recording a confidence level for each record
- Deploy camera traps and acoustic recorders at survey stations to the protocol's height, orientation and settings, recording station metadata
- Measure temperature, pH, dissolved oxygen, conductivity and turbidity in place with field meters calibrated before use and checked afterward
- Collect grab water samples at locations and depths that represent the condition of interest, recording flow and site conditions at collection
- Collect benthic macroinvertebrate, algae or fish community samples from a stream reach following the program's habitat-allocation protocol
- Describe a soil profile's horizons, colour, texture, structure and coarse fragments in standard terminology on the program's description form
- Collect soil samples at specified depths and locations for laboratory analysis of texture, nutrients, carbon or contaminants
- Identify regional plants and animals to species with dichotomous keys and diagnostic features, collecting evidence for any record not identified with certainty
- Accept, correct or reject AI-suggested species identifications against the specimen, image or recording, recording the diagnostic reason for each change

*Credential gates (issuer verified):* 1 not shown until the issuer is verified

## EMST role: Conservation corps member (state variant, entry level; P1)

*Match:* `skos:relatedMatch`, confidence 0.35, unreviewed agent draft (`emst-x5-tx:R01-conservation-corps-member/state:2688`). *Authority position (editorial):* service-provider.

**Competency targets at this level (editorial draft target levels, agent-drafted)**

- Implement ecological restoration treatments and adapt them to site response — entry L1
- Construct and maintain trails to sustainable design standards — entry L1
- Detect, treat and monitor invasive species in the field — entry L1
- Install and maintain erosion control and watershed treatments — entry L1
- Use and maintain hand tools safely for field work — entry L1
- Operate chainsaws and other power equipment safely in field conditions — entry L1
- Manage risk in uncontrolled field environments — entry L1
- Navigate and travel safely in remote terrain with and without digital aids — entry L1
- Provide first aid and emergency medical care in remote field settings — entry L1
- Communicate during field emergencies and report incidents — entry L1
- Apply field biosecurity and decontamination protocols — entry L1
- Record field observations with protocol fidelity and data integrity — entry L1
- Drive and operate field vehicles safely on unpaved roads and off road — entry L1
- Apply safety practices and stop-work authority across field, facility and incident settings — entry L1
- Interpret and question environmental data products in everyday work — entry L1
- Use AI tools responsibly in everyday environmental work — entry L1
- Validate AI-generated work products before professional use — entry L1
- Record provenance and AI involvement in work products — entry L1

**Main tasks at this level (agent draft, in record order)**

*% time: set by the supervisor; EMST supplies none before job analysis.*

*Critical and needed-at-entry tasks: Assessment pending (job analysis).*

- Install native plantings and seedings to the treatment specification, selecting microsites and handling stock so that it survives transplanting
- Build low-tech process-based structures such as beaver dam analogues or post-assisted log structures, placing each from field reading of flow and channel form
- Operate seed drills, tree planters or mulch blowers to the treatment specification, calibrating application rates before each unit
- Build wildlife habitat features such as brush piles, nest structures and pollinator plantings to the design specification for the target species
- Treat invasive plants by mechanical, chemical or biological methods to the treatment prescription, protecting non-target vegetation and water
- Survey high-risk pathways such as trailheads, boat launches and road corridors for new invasive species, recording absences as well as detections
- Install check dams, wattles or silt fences to the specification, keying and anchoring each so that flow cannot undercut or bypass it
- Inspect erosion controls after storm events, repairing or redesigning any that failed and recording the failure mode
- Construct trail tread to the design grade, outslope and width from a flagged alignment, reading soils and drainage along the segment
- Maintain existing trails by clearing drainage structures, brushing corridors and repairing tread before damage spreads
- Build rock structures such as steps, retaining walls or armored crossings to the specification, selecting and setting stone found on site
- Use hand tools such as grubbing hoes, axes, crosscut saws and shovels for vegetation, trail and restoration work with safe spacing and body position

*Credential gates (issuer verified):* 1 not shown until the issuer is verified
